batch_strategy: Measure missing response segments around newly exposed failures, test scaffold-specific loading effects, and challenge transfer into compact neutral chemistry. The 32 selections remain fixed to the supplied premeasurement predictions. Observed evidence IDs appear only in the hypotheses' typed evidence lists; H5 is explicitly an untested hypothesis based on chemical prior and model behavior.

choices.reason: m159 at 10/1, 50 uL tests the currently predicted compact interval, 8.04/17.50 mL, against its matched 5/1 anchor. Following the severe historical 50/1 failure summarized in H1, this determines whether substantial growth starts at 10/1 or occurs later.

m159 at 20/1, 100 uL connects directly to its measured 50/1 endpoint at identical loading. Its prediction of 25.51/49.63 mL makes this an informative transition point between compact low-ratio behavior and the late, broad endpoint documented in H1.

m199 at 5/1, 150 uL supplies the missing fixed-loading predecessor to its recent 10/1 failure. Together with the existing 5/1 loading references listed in H1, it separates a ratio transition from a loading-dependent explanation of that failure.

m120 at 2/1, 150 uL precedes its measured 5/1 row at the same loading. The predicted 13.23/26.52 mL interval tests whether the early onset and broad finish documented in H2 emerge together or through different endpoint responses.

m120 at 5/1, 50 uL creates a loading contrast with its measured 150 uL row, holding the other recorded conditions fixed. This tests whether the broad interval is shared across loading levels or whether loading changes onset and finish differently.

m141 at 5/1, 50 uL pairs with its measured 150 uL row. The 10/1 loading references in H2 show a much larger onset than finish difference. This tests whether that endpoint asymmetry is already present at 5/1 or develops mainly at the weaker eluent.

m191 at 5/1, 150 uL extends its matched 2/1 anchor. Its recent 10/1, 100 uL result was later than predicted. This intermediate label helps locate the dialdehyde transition while retaining loading differences in comparisons with the 10/1 measurement.

m178 at 5/1, 100 uL fills the low side of its fixed-loading curve already measured at 10/1, 20/1 and 50/1. It tests whether the diaryl diketone's late response begins gradually or follows a delayed transition, improving the condition response beyond its high-ratio anchors.

m177 at 50/1, 100 uL challenges the compact predicted extension of the nitro diaryl ketone. H3 contains a compact 20/1 reference and a contrasting late nitrile diaryl ketone. Loading and loading-solvent conditions differ across references, so this tests conditional graph transfer without isolating the nitro-group effect.

m104 at 5/1, 100 uL tests the predicted rise before its compact measured 50/1 anchor. Alongside the selected 20/1 point, it distinguishes a shallow or nonmonotonic methyl-anthranilate response from a compact high-ratio record that should not govern the whole curve.

m104 at 20/1, 100 uL completes a matched 5/1–20/1–50/1 experiment. The ethyl analog reference in H3 is substantially later at 20/1, although loading differs. This tests where ester-alkyl transfer should stop rather than assuming similar polarity counts imply similar response.

m156 at 50/1, 50 uL is predicted at 15.18/34.24 mL despite lacking conventional H-bonding sites. Its high CW distance and predicted onset growth motivate testing whether this fluorinated aromatic graph genuinely needs a late-onset response or receives an inappropriate transferred correction.

m71 in pure EA, 100 uL tests the unusual predicted late, narrow interval of 10.85/11.76 mL. Current weaker-eluent predictions at the same loading have earlier onsets. This challenges an inverse predicted condition response in a highly hydrophobic thiophene without assuming the experimental direction.

m18 at 2/1, 100 uL pairs with its selected pure-EA row. The predictor places onset later at 2/1 than at 50/1 under the same loading conditions. This tests whether the long-chain acrylate supports that nonmonotonic response or inherits an inappropriate structural correction.

m18 in pure EA, 100 uL currently has an unordered point prediction: V1 8.25 mL exceeds V2 8.10 mL. A label here, paired with the selected 2/1 point, can repair endpoint consistency and test whether the predicted delayed onset has experimental support.

m45 at 20/1, 100 uL lies between the positive 10/1 measurement and the unordered near-zero 50/1 record listed in H4. Its prediction also falls below the measured 10/1 endpoints. This bounds the anomalous region without interpreting negative recorded V2 as a physical retention mechanism.

m173 at 1/1, 100 uL with 2000 uL DCM loading fills a fixed-condition gap between its pure-EA and 2/1 measurements. Those references already have broad finishes. This supplies an acid-specific endpoint-shape reference while the m45 extreme record remains unresolved.

Molecule-novel isoamyl benzoate m55 at 20/1, 100 uL begins a matched two-ratio experiment. Related isobutyl benzoate evidence listed in H3 anchors solvent sensitivity in the homologous family. The extra methylene tests transfer across common neutral ester graphs.

m55 at 40/1, 100 uL pairs with its selected 20/1 point with all other recorded conditions fixed. The predicted change from 7.14/16.35 to 9.57/22.72 mL tests a response slope, separating a new-scaffold offset from condition sensitivity.

Molecule-novel meta-bromopropiophenone m64 at 50/1, 100 uL pairs with the selected fluoro analog m65. Lower-ratio halogenated-ketone references are listed in H3. Density and loading mass differ between analogs, so the comparison remains conditional rather than isolating halogen identity.

m65 at 50/1, 100 uL extends its accurately predicted 5/1 anchor. Its pairing with m64 tests whether ordinary halogenated ketones share the predicted moderate weak-eluent response, helping bound corrections learned from much later pyridyl and nitrile ketones.

Molecule-novel bromo-trifluoromethyl benzaldehyde m187 at 10/1, 100 uL starts a matched two-ratio test. The compact dibromobenzaldehyde reference listed in H3 is a relevant, imperfect structural analogy. This probes carbonyl environment and substitution beyond acceptor counts.

m187 at 50/1, 100 uL pairs with its selected 10/1 point. The predictor gives little onset movement, 5.21 to 5.61 mL, with a more noticeable finish change. Measuring both endpoints tests whether this new aldehyde supports that shallow response or requires a scaffold-specific transition.

Molecule-novel bromo-chlorobenzaldehyde m192 at 50/1, 100 uL tests transfer within the substituted aldehyde family alongside m187. Its related positional-isomer reference in H3 is at lower ratio and different loading. This adds a weak-eluent structural boundary without claiming an isolated positional effect.

m117 at 50/1, 150 uL extends matched 1/1 and 5/1 records with finishes near 20 mL. It tests whether methoxy substitution preserves a shallow hydroxy-aldehyde response or permits the later finish predicted in weak eluent.

m197 at 20/1, 100 uL precedes its matched 50/1 measurement. Its current prediction retains an early onset and roughly 30 mL finish before that later endpoint. This locates late growth separately from the broad finishes already observed at lower ratios.

m106 at 20/1, 100 uL extends its measured 10/1 record with only PE/EA changing. Large predictor quantile widths reinforce the value of testing the predicted 27.28/58.44 mL interval. The label informs solvent sensitivity of a flexible ether-ketone environment.

m94 at 10/1, 50 uL extends its matched 1/1 record and pairs with the selected 20/1 row. Related beta-ketoester references in H3 show substantial condition responses. This tests transfer to the cyclopropyl carbonyl environment.

m94 at 20/1, 50 uL completes the matched ratio pair, predicted at 22.91/53.24 mL versus 16.85/34.69 mL at 10/1. These labels distinguish a genuine accelerating beta-ketoester response from a broad-response correction transferred from related scaffolds.

m80 at 20/1, 100 uL tests a predicted transition to 18.56/41.23 mL. Its measured 5/1 and 10/1 references remain compact at other loading levels. This asks whether the diester response rises sharply after 10/1 rather than assuming four acceptors imply broad retention everywhere.

m80 at 50/1, 100 uL pairs exactly with its selected 20/1 row and tests the further predicted rise to 31.56/76.18 mL. Measuring both points distinguishes a real late transition from extrapolation driven by related multifunctional esters.

Molecule-novel ethyl bromopropionate m77 at 10/1, 150 uL tests transfer across alpha branching and ester alkyl identity. Related bromoester references listed in H3 provide compact anchors. This supplies a common neutral-chemistry boundary alongside the polar transition experiments.

hypotheses.content: Increasing PE/EA can produce delayed, nonlinear growth of V1 and V2, with transition location and endpoint shape depending on scaffold. The previous plateau interpretation for m199 is unsupported by its newly measured 10/1 result; its loading dependence remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate and paired ratio labels distinguish a misplaced transition from a molecule-wide offset. They can improve condition sensitivity without extending late-retention corrections to every condition or forcing both endpoints to follow the same shape.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do m159 and m199 leave their compact or moderate regimes, and are the predicted transitions for m80 and m94 experimentally supported?

hypotheses.content: Loading responses can affect onset and finish differently, and their magnitude may depend on both scaffold and PE/EA. Existing contrasts support endpoint asymmetry but do not establish a universal causal loading rule.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading contrasts teach separate V1 and V2 responses and help prevent one scaffold's loading direction from being transferred to unrelated rows. They also help distinguish broad elution intervals from simple retention shifts.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m120 retain its early onset and broad finish at lower loading, and is m141's onset-specific loading contrast already present at 5/1?

hypotheses.content: Functional-group environment and graph topology govern how retention corrections transfer. Neutral carbonyls, acids, amino esters and related homologs need distinct condition responses even when coarse polarity descriptors are similar; individual structural mechanisms remain untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Related-graph experiments identify where broad or late-retention corrections should transfer and where they should stop. Compact references can protect common neutral rows while response pairs teach scaffold offsets separately from solvent sensitivity.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m104 curve, m64/m65 comparison, m55 homolog response, and substituted aldehyde experiments preserve the predicted structural boundaries?

hypotheses.content: Some extreme or unordered recorded outcomes may reflect unresolved row variability or label conventions rather than a transferable chromatographic mechanism. The cause cannot be identified from the supplied variables alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: An isolated anomalous label can otherwise induce an inappropriate solvent or loading correction over many rows. Nearby labels help constrain the conditional surface and expose limits to smooth mechanistic interpretation, although they cannot resolve missing metadata.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m45 at 20/1 remain positive and ordered, continue growing from 10/1, or show a decrease before the anomalous 50/1 record?

hypotheses.content: Current predictions for m156, m18 and m71 may overtransfer late-onset responses or misrepresent solvent effects. The unordered m18 pure-EA prediction and the inverse predicted responses for the hydrophobic compounds warrant measurement. Competition by EA for silica interactions is a chemical prior, not evidence of these compounds' actual response directions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These experiments challenge structural extrapolation and endpoint inconsistency in regions complementary to the polar, late-eluting failures. Paired conditions can distinguish an incorrect onset offset from an incorrect solvent-response shape.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m156 develop a late onset at 50/1, and do m18 and m71 support the predicted delayed onset in stronger eluent?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes redirect attention toward transition location and endpoint shape. m159 at 50/1 and m199 at 10/1 had historical V2 underpredictions of about 83 and 69 mL, respectively. These results overturn a compact extrapolation for m159 and the proposed plateau for m199. The retrained predictor has already changed, so those errors are acquisition-time feedback, not current residuals. Recent m141 intermediate points and the m37 low-loading 20/1 result confirm substantial solvent responses with smaller recent misses, reducing the value of further sampling their established high-ratio endpoints. m120 presents a different failure: onset was earlier and finish later than predicted, motivating a loading contrast and a preceding ratio point. The m19 midpoint supports an onset-specific loading trend, and m205's third loading level continues finish growth with little additional onset movement; both local series now have enough coverage to shift effort elsewhere. For m202, the new 5/1 pair has almost identical finishes near 13 mL, so its broad 100 uL record at 10/1 does not establish a general mass effect. The new m195 low-loading result is close to its 100 uL result and leaves the unordered 150 uL record unresolved. The negative V2 for m45 at 50/1 similarly cannot justify a physical collapse mechanism. Compact results for ordinary halogenated ketones and an ester reinforce the need to bound transfer from broad polar failures. H5 has no observed-evidence citations and remains an untested chemical-prior/model-behavior proposal.
batch_rationale:
The batch measures response segments with identifiable learning questions. m159, m199, m120 and m191 address newly exposed failure regions; the loading contrasts for m120 and m141 test endpoint-specific condition interactions. Matched ratio pairs for m55, m187, m94 and m80 distinguish scaffold offsets from solvent sensitivity. The m104 curve tests a consequential boundary between related amino esters, while m177, halogenated ketones, substituted aldehydes and m77 constrain how corrections transfer into compact neutral rows. These selections should teach relationships that recur across the Row-distribution rather than simply add extreme labels.

The m156, m18 and m71 experiments challenge suspicious predictions, including an unordered point prediction. The adjacent m45 experiment bounds an anomalous recorded region, with the m173 label providing an acid-specific reference. Comparisons with unmatched loading or loading-solvent volumes remain conditional evidence rather than isolated causal effects. Quantile widths and CW distances provide secondary evidence; single-predictor quantile widths are not assumed to be calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Experimental V2 minus V1 remains a target interval width. The batch includes potentially broad transitions and compact controls so retraining can improve both endpoints without imposing a blanket broadening or retention correction.
